findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the bare-`rebar review <id>` semantic flip (now signs an attestation / enforces the blocking floor) is an intentional immediate cutover, and either add an opt-out/back-out note for scripted callers or explicitly document that the deprecation stderr line names the new write side-effect (not just the removal).
evidence: 'Turn rebar review into a loud deprecation shim over review-plan'
AC5: 'plan-review signs an attestation, enforces a blocking floor, fast-fails with no LLM on a non-claimable ticket'
T4 rule: 'checking only that breakage is acknowledged is insufficient; require the reversibility mechanism'
The library/MCP surfaces DO get expand-contract (kept + deprecated + remove_in v1.0.0); the CLI verb's semantics flip immediately with no opt-in
findings.finding: The CLI verb `rebar review <id>` (invoked bare, with no rejected argument) is directly repurposed to run the multi-pass plan-review gate, which SIGNS AN ATTESTATION and enforces a blocking floor — a write/state side-effect the retired single-pass read-only review did not have. Existing scripted callers passing only an id get this new side-effect with no opt-out flag. The plan documents the four behavioral differences (AC5) but T4 treats documentation/acknowledgement of a breaking behavior change as insufficient without an explicit expand-contract or rollback/back-out path; the CLI verb is not expand-contracted the way the library/MCP surfaces are.
scenarios: A CI script runs `rebar review <id>` expecting a read-only single-pass verdict and instead signs an attestation and blocks on the floor
An operator scripting bulk `rebar review` calls hits the plan-review fast-fail on non-claimable tickets
findings.suggested_fix: Add to Approach move 1 an explicit note that the shim's deprecation stderr message names the new side effects (attestation signing + blocking floor), and record the intentional-immediate-cutover decision with its rollback = revert-the-shim rationale, so the breaking behavior change is a justified choice rather than incidental.
